schema.$comment: Open to fields a newer producer adds (SPEC §9). Derived from `records.rs`'s field map by `vocabulary()`; edit the map, not this.

record_index.description: An ordering key over the records of one Map Creator file. A whole number, never negative, and never above 2^53 − 1: a key travels as a JSON number and is read back by consumers whose numbers are IEEE doubles, where every integer up to 2^53 is exact and the next one is not — so a larger key can come back as a different key, and two records can come back with one key between them.

mapcreator_aisle.description: How `vtm_zone.json` wrote the aisle record this entity is, beyond what the record says about the site.

index.description: The record's ordering key in its Map Creator file: bigger means later. A lens list comes back in identity order and the identities are random, so the order a file states its records in is a fact this document carries. The values are gapped rather than consecutive so that inserting a record between two others takes a value between theirs and leaves every other record's key alone — a re-import is a diff, and renumbering a file would rewrite every entity of it.

io_point_coordinates_as_pairs.description: The places in Map Creator's `io_point_coordinates`, counting from zero, of the entries that name a cell by a raw grid pair such as `[6, 1]` rather than by the coordinate string `"[6,1]"`, so the export writes each back as the file spelled it. Absent when every entry is a string.

key_order.description: The order the file wrote the keys of an object of this record in, for each object whose order is not the one the export entity's `key_orders` gives an object with the same keys at the same place, by its JSON pointer from the record's own object (`""` for that object; on the export entity, which holds what lies outside every record, the file's name and its pointer in the file). JSON gives key order no meaning; the export writes each file back byte for byte, so the order is a fact this document carries.

written_negative_zero.description: The JSON pointers, from the record's own object (on the export entity, the file's name and the pointer in the file), of the zeros the file wrote with a minus sign (`-0.0`), which a reader holds as the zero without one, so that the export writes them back with one.

written_with_point.description: The JSON pointers, from the record's own object (on the export entity, the file's name and the pointer in the file), of the whole numbers the file wrote with a decimal point (`40.0`), which a reader spells as integers, so that the export writes them back with one.

A lens list comes back in identity order and the identities are random, so the order a file states its records in is a fact this document carries. The values are gapped rather than consecutive so that inserting a record between two others takes a value between theirs and leaves every other record's key alone — a re-import is a diff, and renumbering a file would rewrite every entity of it.

key_order.description: The order the file wrote the keys of an object of this record in, for each object whose order is not the one the export entity's `key_orders` gives an object with the same keys at the same place, by its JSON pointer from the record's own object (`""` for that object; on the export entity, which holds what lies outside every record, the file's name and its pointer in the file). JSON gives key order no meaning; the export writes each file back byte for byte, so the order is a fact this document carries.

written_negative_zero.description: The JSON pointers, from the record's own object (on the export entity, the file's name and the pointer in the file), of the zeros the file wrote with a minus sign (`-0.0`), which a reader holds as the zero without one, so that the export writes them back with one.

written_with_point.description: The JSON pointers, from the record's own object (on the export entity, the file's name and the pointer in the file), of the whole numbers the file wrote with a decimal point (`40.0`), which a reader spells as integers, so that the export writes them back with one.
